name: Policy Gradient Methods
description: Policy Gradient methods directly optimize the policy (action selection probabilities) by estimating gradients of expected cumulative reward. Unlike value-based methods, they can handle continuous action spaces and naturally explore through stochastic policies. The policy is typically represented by a neural network.

concept.policyRepresentation: π(a|s,θ) - probability of action given state and parameters
concept.policyGradient: ∇J(θ) = E[∇log π(a|s,θ) × G] where G is return
concept.scoreFunction: ∇log π(a|s,θ) - how to increase action probability
concept.baseline: Subtract baseline to reduce variance (e.g., value function)
concept.explanation: Increase probability of actions that lead to high returns, decrease for low returns. Gradient ascent on policy parameters.

idealScenarios: Complex policies where value function hard to learn
avoidWhen: Environments with sparse rewards (hard to credit)

learningRate.impact: Too high: unstable; too low: slow convergence

episodes.impact: Policy gradient typically needs many episodes

algorithms.reinforce: Monte Carlo policy gradient (full episode returns)
algorithms.actorCritic: Combine policy gradient with value function estimation
algorithms.ppo: Proximal Policy Optimization - clipped surrogate objective
algorithms.trpo: Trust Region Policy Optimization - constrained updates

initialization: Optionally initialize value function V(s) for baseline
episodeCollection: Run full episode with current policy
Compute returns Gₜ for each timestep (discounted sum of future rewards)
gradientUpdate: Compute log probabilities of taken actions
Calculate advantage: A = G - V(s) (if using baseline)
convergence: KL divergence between old and new policy (for TRPO/PPO)

complexity.scalability: Good with GPUs; parallel environments (A3C) speed up
complexity.interpretability: Low - neural policy is black box

pros: Can learn complex policies with neural networks
Better convergence properties than Q-learning for some problems
cons: Local optima (policy gradient is hill climbing)
May converge to suboptimal deterministic policy

varianceReduction.baseline: Subtract state value V(s) from return
varianceReduction.advantage: A(s,a) = Q(s,a) - V(s) - how much better than average
